findings.source_quote: φήμη τις ἠρέμα ἐπὶ τῆς Τιβερίου Καίσαρος βασιλείας ἐξ ἐαρινῆς τροπῆς τὴν ἀρχὴν λαμβάνουσα ηὔξανεν ἑκάστοτε
findings.english_quote: a report arose quietly during the reign of Tiberius Caesar. Taking its beginning from the spring equinox, it kept growing from time to time
findings.issue: The draft attaches ἠρέμα to an introduced act of arising rather than to the report’s growth. The Greek describes a report beginning at the spring turning point and growing quietly or gradually.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep ἠρέμα with the growth: for example, “a report, beginning at the spring equinox during the reign of Tiberius Caesar, kept growing quietly.” Review the rendering of ἑκάστοτε alongside its repetition in the following sentence.

findings.source_quote: καὶ ὡς ἀληθῶς ἀγαθὴ θεοῦ ἄγγελος διέτρεχε τὸν κόσμον
findings.english_quote: and, like a truly good messenger from God, traveled throughout the world
findings.issue: ὡς ἀληθῶς is the idiomatic expression “in truth” or “truly.” The draft instead makes ὡς introduce a comparison and makes “truly” qualify the messenger’s goodness. This weakens the identification of the personified report as God’s good messenger.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “and, truly a good messenger of God, it ran throughout the world.” Retain the personification without implying that the report is necessarily a celestial being. The replacement requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: Ἰουδαίοις τὴν. τοῦ ἀιδίου θεοῦ εὐαγγελίζεται βασιλείαν
findings.english_quote: was proclaiming to the Jews the kingdom of the eternal God
findings.issue: Generic “proclaiming” leaves the good-news force of εὐαγγελίζεται unexpressed. The separately disclosed printed stop after τὴν is an editorial punctuation feature, not evidence that the Greek wording is corrupt.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “was announcing to the Jews the good news of the eternal God’s kingdom.” Keep the printed punctuation disclosure separate from this lexical revision; no Greek emendation is proposed.

findings.english_quote: Preserves the abstract noun θεότης and the image of being filled with it.
findings.issue: The lexical note identifies the wrong lemma. θειότητος is the genitive of θειότης, not θεότης. The main rendering “full of divinity” does not itself require replacement on this account.
findings.suggested_revision: Correct the note to identify θειότης. Do not infer a theological contrast with θεότης merely from the different word forms.

findings.english_quote: Even lepers and those with scabies
findings.issue: “Scabies” selects a specific diagnosis where ψωροί can describe an itching or scabby condition more broadly. The asyndetic wording also permits uncertainty about whether two groups are being listed or ψωροί further describes the lepers. The note presents distinguishable descriptions without preserving that alternative.
findings.suggested_revision: Prefer a broader description such as “people with leprosy and scabby skin conditions,” with a note that the supplied asyndetic phrase may instead describe a single group of scabby lepers. Review both the grouping and medical terminology before accepting revised wording.

findings.issue: The civic address is retained, but the explicit address to men is lost.
findings.suggested_revision: Use “Men of Rome, listen!” or “Roman men, listen!”

findings.issue: “Inexpressible” selects inability to express the benefits. ἀπόρρητα also supports the sense “secret” or “not to be divulged.” The note mentions things not to be spoken but does not give a concrete alternative rendering, and this context does not securely settle the distinction.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “his unutterable good things,” accompanied by explicit alternatives such as “his secret or undisclosed good things” and “his inexpressible good things.” Any replacement remains subject to fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ὡς ὅτι υἱὸς θεοῦ ἐπιδεδήμηκεν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ
findings.english_quote: For the Son of God had come to Judea
findings.issue: The draft closes the imagined response before this clause and makes it a direct causal assertion by the narrator. The attachment of ὡς ὅτι and the extent of the imagined quotation remain uncertain: the clause may explain the reported announcement or continue the imagined response. The existing note acknowledges uncertainty about the connector but does not disclose this quotation-scope alternative. A printed sentence stop does not by itself establish the end of direct speech.
findings.suggested_revision: Reassess the quotation boundary and preserve the reporting possibility. A connective such as “namely, that the Son of God has come to Judea” is a candidate for review, not an accepted replacement. Explicitly document the alternative explanatory or quoted attachment. This is an unresolved interpretive issue, not demonstrated source corruption requiring another print transcription.

findings.english_quote: by entangling those who are eager to act in hope, it lies in wait for them
findings.issue: The English can attach “in hope” to being eager to act, whereas ἐλπίδι describes the means or circumstance of entanglement. “To act” also narrows the unspecified eagerness or haste of τοὺς σπεύδοντας.
findings.suggested_revision: Make hope’s role in the trap explicit: for example, “it lies in ambush for those who hurry, entangling them with hope.” Review “those who hurry” against “the eager” before accepting the replacement.

findings.source_quote: ὃν ποτε εἰσεκλάπην χρόνον ἐλπίσιν δονούμενος
findings.english_quote: I also considered how much time I had somehow been drawn in unawares, tossed about by hopes
findings.issue: The draft properly discloses uncertainty about εἰσεκλάπην, but “how much time” introduces a quantitative emphasis not explicitly expressed by ὃν χρόνον, and “somehow” gives ποτε a manner sense rather than its temporal or indefinite force. These choices should not be treated as settled consequences of the difficult construction.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “I also reflected on the time during which I had been beguiled, tossed about by hopes,” retaining a note that “beguiled” or “drawn in” and the relation of the accusative of time remain tentative. Do not alter εἰσεκλάπην or classify unfamiliar grammar as a transcription error. Revised English needs fresh review.
